title: Common definitions
description: Shared vocabulary for the file spec's documents. Referenced by $ref; never instantiated directly.

digest.description: A sha256 digest in OCI notation: the literal prefix sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hex characters. File spec section 4.1.

namespace.description: Owner segment of a ref. Lowercase DNS-label grammar, 1 to 64 characters. File spec section 2.1.

kind.description: Kind segment of a ref. Lowercase identifier, underscores allowed, 1 to 32 characters. File spec section 2.1.

name.description: Name segment of a ref. Same grammar as namespace. File spec section 2.1.

version.description: A version string. Semantic versioning SHOULD be used. The literal 'latest' is reserved and invalid. File spec section 2.1.

ref.description: A fully qualified artifact reference: namespace/kind/name@version.

status.description: Lifecycle status of a version. Which transitions are legal is a server concern and is not defined by the file spec.

format_version.description: Storage format version, opted into per root. This schema describes version 1. Readers refuse values they do not understand.

capability.description: What a root offers. A format 1 file root advertises files. The other values are reserved for a future server.

labels.description: Short, indexable key/value pairs. Part of the version: covered by the content digest and fixed once released.

annotations.description: Free-form key/value pairs that are stored but never indexed. Part of the version, like labels.

root_url.description: An HTTPS root: an origin plus an optional opaque path prefix, written without a trailing slash. File spec sections 1, 3.1 and 8.

auth.description: How to authenticate against a root or a host. type none means anonymous reading. File spec section 7.

resource_metadata.description: RFC 9728 protected resource metadata URL. Required when type is oauth2, and the same URL the 401 challenge names.

login_url.description: Where an interactive client sends a person to obtain a token.

page.description: Paging envelope for a roots_url response. Cursors are opaque. File spec section 8.
